correctness.rationale: The published paperfolding theorem gives a global maximum factor length 45 for words admitting repetition factorizations. In the four-letter 2-uniform fixed point, factor sets of μ^9(0) and μ^10(0) agree through length 45. Any factor of μ(z) of length ℓ≤45 depends on a source factor of length at most ceil((ℓ+1)/2)≤23 and one parity offset, proving by induction no later factors appear at length ≤45. Coding yields a complete regular binary bounded factor language. Exact dynamic programming over every admissible prefix with period ≤ half its length finds 232 distinct factorizable factors, counts {1:112,2:94,3:12,4:2,5:10,6:2}, shortest ambiguous length 9 (four factors), longest unique length 30 (two), maximal multiplicity 6 (two). Distinct factors, not occurrences, are counted; the global cutoff is essential.

evidence: The global length cutoff is prior and makes full finite census possible.
